text:
There are countries I remember

as I remember my childhoods.

They are countries of sea or river,

of pastures, meadows, and waters.

My village beside the Rhône,

surrendered to river and cicadas;

Antilles in green-black palms

that lie halfway out to sea and call me;

Lig urian rock of Portofino,

Italian sea, Italian sea!


They have brought me to a country without rivers,

lands of Hagar, lands without water;

white Saras and red Saras,

where other races sinned,

with the red sin of the Atreids

that slashed clays recount;

that were not born like a child

with plump little bodies,

when I hear them, without a whistle,

when I cross them, without a glance.


I want to return to childhood lands;

carry me to a gentle country of waters.

Let me grow old in great pastures

and make the river fable upon fable.

Let a spring be my mother,

and let me seek her at siesta,

and let sweet water descend in jars

from a crag, sharp and rough.


May the fierce, icy water

overcome me and stop my breath.

May it break my cup, and as I drink,

make my insides young again!

translation.title: There are countries I remember...
